item.title: Life in the theatre is most revealing | Letters
item.summary: Cathy Scott-Willars responds to an article about the secret lives of theatre workers I enjoyed your article ( The secret lives of theatre workers: ‘People were having full sex in the stalls’, 9 August ). I worked many roles front of house and later as operations manager at a busy regional theatre, and it has provided me with some of the most entertaining stories. My favourite was working at a performance of The Rocky Horror Show in the large main theatre, while in the smaller studio was a play aimed at teenagers. The programming team had provided some post-show entertainment in the form of a DJ and breakdancer for the studio show, which happened to time with the interval of Rocky Horror. The scene I was met with was an usher crying, a furious college tutor shouting at her because her students had witnessed a man in a corset and thong attempt breakdancing, and his balls had fallen out, exposing himself.
